text:
olivia: Hey team — PR #8487 is ready for merge from my side but it's gated on the architecture sign-off per the RFC. RFC link: https://rwd.im/rfc-210-kv-routing. TL;DR: introduce a routing tier that prefers cached shards for low-latency requests; impacts autoscaling and fallback logic.

olivia: PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8487 (changes in router + canary policy). I added a short checklist in the PR description for risk areas.

sam: taking a look now. quick question: does this change require any infra config migration?

olivia: not a schema migration. there's a config flag `router.use_shard_affinity` that defaults to false; we'll flip it in the canary. docs updated in the PR.

anika: thanks — can you call out the perf numbers (p95 token latency) for canary vs current in the PR? need that for PM and SRE.

olivia: added a small table in the PR comment: 95th down ~18% on short sequences when affinity enabled, throughput neutral. I'll paste the bench command too: `./scripts/bench --model redwood-7b --seq 128 --mode routing`.

cheng: RFC note: section 3.2 mentions fallback to smaller quantized variant when shard unavailable. does PR implement that?

olivia: yes, fallback hook is wired to model-variant routing. there's a unit test and an integration test in `test/routing/fallback_test.py` — CI passed.

ci-bot: build #12987 for PR 8487 — ✅ all checks passed. :white_check_mark:

maya: quick design ask — can we ensure the canary window is configurable per-customer in case Dedicated customers want a longer soak? If not, add to the rollout plan.

olivia: good call. I added `rollout.canary_duration` in the config with a default of `1h` and documented per-tenant override.

sam: i'm mostly 👍, but tagging @cheng for final architecture stamp. cheng — do you want a brief call or can you review inline? :eyes:

cheng: inline is fine. i flagged one comment about shard affinity and cold-start KV priming. please add an integration test that simulates an empty KV cache and measures priming latency.

olivia: on it — adding the test now. should be done today. will link the new commit.

anika: once cheng signs off, can we do a controlled canary: 5% traffic for 6 hours then 25% for 24h? needs to be in the rollout plan for product acceptance.

olivia: noted. plan added to PR description under "rollout plan".

cheng: left one more nit on doc string in `router.go` but that's optional. overall LGTM after the KV priming test.

olivia: thanks — will push the test and request final review. if cheng gives OK I'll schedule the merge during the low-traffic window tomorrow morning.

maya: thanks for running the perf numbers and adding the opts. ping me when you start the canary and i'll coordinate with SRE on runbooks.

olivia: will do. pinging again once the test is in. :thumbsup:
